subject_intro: How much of the Personal Allowance a lower-earning spouse or civil partner can transfer, and the most it can cut the couple's tax bill each year.
subject_meta_title: Marriage Allowance 2026/27: £1,260 Transfer, Up to £252 Saving
subject_meta_description: Marriage Allowance for 2026/27: transfer £1,260 of your Personal Allowance to a basic rate spouse or civil partner and cut their tax by up to £252.
label: Amount you can transfer
context: The lower earner gives up this much of their Personal Allowance, and it reduces their spouse or civil partner's taxable income.

label: Most it can save each year
context: The receiving partner's tax falls by up to this much in the tax year. Claims can be backdated to 6 April 2022.
The lower earner normally needs income below this for the couple to benefit.
The receiving partner must normally have income below this, so they pay no more than the basic rate. In Scotland the limit is £43,662.

label: Blind Person's Allowance
context: Added to the Personal Allowance for people who are blind or severely sight impaired. Any unused part can go to a spouse or civil partner.

subcategory_description: Tax-free allowances for side income, and the Making Tax Digital rules for sole traders and landlords.
subject_name: Trading, Property and Rent a Room Allowances
subject_intro: The tax-free allowances for small amounts of income from self-employment, renting out property, and letting a furnished room in your own home.
subject_meta_title: Trading, Property and Rent a Room Allowances 2026/27
subject_meta_description: The £1,000 trading and property allowances and the £7,500 Rent a Room limit: how much side income from selling, freelancing or letting is tax-free.
label: Trading allowance
context: Gross income from self-employment or casual work up to this each tax year is tax-free, and you don't need to register for Self Assessment.

label: Property allowance
context: Gross income from land or property up to this each tax year is tax-free. Above it, you can deduct £1,000 instead of your actual expenses.

label: Rent a Room limit
context: You can earn up to this each year tax-free from letting furnished accommodation in your own home, whether you own it or rent it.

label: Rent a Room limit if you share the income
context: The limit is halved if you share the rental income with someone else.

subject_name: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
subject_intro: When sole traders and landlords must keep digital records and send quarterly updates to HMRC, based on their income from self-employment and property.
subject_meta_title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: Thresholds and Start Dates
subject_meta_description: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies from April 2026 above £50,000 of self-employment and property income, then above £30,000 from 2027 and £20,000 from 2028.
label: Income threshold from 6 April 2026
context: Applies if your self-employment and property income, before expenses, was over this in the 2024/25 tax year.

label: Income threshold from 6 April 2027
context: Applies if your self-employment and property income, before expenses, is over this in the 2025/26 tax year.

label: Income threshold from 6 April 2028
context: Applies if your self-employment and property income, before expenses, is over this in the 2026/27 tax year.

subject_intro: How much you can give away each year free of Inheritance Tax, the extra allowances for wedding gifts, and how gifts are taxed if you die within 7 years.
subject_meta_title: Inheritance Tax Gift Allowances and the 7-Year Rule
subject_meta_description: Inheritance Tax gift rules: the £3,000 annual exemption, £250 small gifts, wedding gifts up to £5,000, and taper relief on gifts made 3 to 7 years before death.
label: Annual exemption
context: The total you can give away each tax year without it counting towards your estate. Any unused amount carries forward one tax year only.

label: Small gift allowance (per person)
context: You can give as many gifts of up to this per person as you like each tax year, as long as no other allowance is used on the same person.

label: Wedding or civil partnership gift to a child
context: Can be combined with the annual exemption for the same person, but not with the small gift allowance.

label: Wedding gift to a grandchild or great-grandchild
context: The tax-free limit for a gift to a grandchild or great-grandchild who is getting married or forming a civil partnership.

label: Wedding gift to anyone else
context: The tax-free limit for a wedding or civil partnership gift to anyone other than a child or grandchild.

label: Years you must live after a gift
context: No Inheritance Tax is due on a gift if you live this long after giving it, unless the gift is part of a trust.

label: Tax on gifts made 3 to 4 years before death
context: Taper relief only applies if gifts made in the 7 years before death total more than the £325,000 threshold.

label: Tax on gifts made 4 to 5 years before death
context: The rate falls the longer you live after making the gift.

label: Tax on gifts made 5 to 6 years before death
context: The rate falls the longer you live after making the gift.

label: Tax on gifts made 6 to 7 years before death
context: After 7 years, no Inheritance Tax is due on the gift.
Gifts made less than 3 years before death are taxed at the full rate.
If gifts in the 7 years before death total more than this, the people who received them pay Inheritance Tax on their gifts.

label: Farm and business property 100% relief allowance
context: From 6 April 2026, qualifying agricultural and business property gets 100% relief up to this amount, and 50% relief above it.

subcategory_description: Corporation Tax rates for companies, and VAT rates and registration thresholds for businesses.
subject_intro: The Corporation Tax rates UK companies pay on their profits, and the profit limits where marginal relief applies between the two rates.
subject_meta_title: Corporation Tax Rates 2026: 19% Small Profits Rate and 25% Main Rate
subject_meta_description: UK Corporation Tax for the year from 1 April 2026: 19% on profits up to £50,000, 25% over £250,000, and marginal relief in between.
label: Small profits rate
context: Paid by companies with profits of £50,000 or less, for the financial year starting 1 April 2026.

label: Main rate
context: Paid by companies with profits over £250,000, for the financial year starting 1 April 2026.

label: Marginal relief lower limit
context: Profits between this and the upper limit are taxed at the main rate, reduced by marginal relief.

label: Marginal relief upper limit
context: Above this, profits are taxed at the full main rate.

subject_intro: The three UK VAT rates, and the taxable turnover at which a business must register for VAT or can apply to cancel its registration.
subject_meta_description: UK VAT: the 20% standard, 5% reduced and 0% zero rates, the £90,000 registration threshold and the £88,000 deregistration threshold.
label: Standard rate
context: Charged on most goods and services. It has been 20% since 4 January 2011.

label: Reduced rate
context: Charged on some goods and services, for example children's car seats and home energy.

label: Zero rate
context: For zero-rated goods and services, for example most food and children's clothes. Exempt items, such as postage stamps, are different.

label: Registration threshold
context: A business must register for VAT if its taxable turnover goes over this. Businesses not established in the UK must register from their first taxable sale.

label: Deregistration threshold
context: A business can apply to cancel its VAT registration if its taxable turnover falls below this.

label: Employment Allowance (yearly)
context: Eligible employers can reduce their annual employer National Insurance bill by up to this.

label: Voluntary Class 3 rate (weekly)
context: A voluntary payment to fill or avoid gaps in your National Insurance record, which counts towards your State Pension.
